record.paper_title: Open problems in billiards and quantitative symplectic geometry
record.original_question: Find real-world systems from areas such as physics, mechanics, biology, or economics that can be modeled as locally conformal symplectic flows or maps, where the symplectic structure is locally rescaled and may encode non-uniform or spatially varying dissipation.

evidence.quote: Find real-world systems ... modeled as LCS flows/maps

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A locally conformal symplectic (LCS) structure on a smooth manifold $M^{2n}$ is a non-degenerate 2-form $\omega$ together with a closed 1-form $\eta$ (the Lee form) satisfying $d\omega = \eta \wedge \omega$. Equivalently, $M$ is covered by open sets $U_\alpha$ on each of which $\omega|_{U_\alpha} = e^{f_\alpha}\omega_\alpha$ for some smooth function $f_\alpha$ and some genuine symplectic form $\omega_\alpha$, with the conformal factors patched together by the cohomology class of $\eta$. An LCS flow (respectively LCS map) is a smooth flow (respectively diffeomorphism) preserving the LCS structure up to local conformal rescaling; infinitesimally, this allows non-uniform, spatially varying contraction or expansion of phase-space volume, generalizing the uniform dissipation rate of conformal (globally conformal) symplectic systems.

Problem. Identify and describe concrete real-world dynamical systems — drawn from physics (e.g., mechanics with non-uniform friction, electromagnetic or acoustic media with spatially varying damping, thermodynamic systems), biology (e.g., population or neural dynamics with heterogeneous dissipation), or economics (e.g., market models with state-dependent damping) — whose continuous-time or discrete-time evolution is naturally modeled by an LCS flow or LCS map with a non-exact Lee form $\eta$. In particular, exhibit explicit choices of $(M,\omega,\eta)$ and the generating Hamiltonian (or diffeomorphism) for which the local conformal factor genuinely depends on the phase-space point, so that the model cannot be reduced to a globally conformal symplectic system.
artifact.status_search_result: The literature contains examples of (globally) conformal symplectic and conformal Hamiltonian systems modeling uniform dissipation — e.g., the Duffing oscillator, damped acoustic waves, and certain optimization dynamics — but no canonical real-world models requiring the strictly locally (non-globally) conformal symplectic setting with a non-exact Lee form have been identified in the searched sources. The question of finding such concrete applied models therefore appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Modelling damped acoustic waves by a dissipation-preserving conformal symplectic method
status_evidence.snippet: Conformal symplectic schemes preserve conformal conservation laws of dissipative wave systems in attenuating media.
status_evidence.claim: Globally conformal symplectic models exist for damped acoustic wave propagation, but these involve uniform damping, not the spatially varying conformal factor characteristic of truly LCS systems.

status_evidence.title: Conformal Hamiltonian systems
status_evidence.snippet: Simple mechanical systems with friction, such as the Duffing oscillator, are conformal Hamiltonian and dissipate symplectic area uniformly.
status_evidence.claim: Known applied examples are conformal (uniform dissipation), leaving the locally conformal (non-uniform) case as an open modeling question.

status_evidence.title: Locally Conformal Symplectic Manifolds
status_evidence.snippet: Foundational reference on LCS geometry; discusses geometric structure but does not provide applied real-world models.
status_evidence.claim: The standard LCS literature is geometric and lacks identified applied dynamical examples.
